chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from al-Hasan ibn Jahm, who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) came out to me, so I found from him an aroma of incense.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, a title for Imam al-Hassan (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّجْمِيرِ: Incense or the act of burning incense

ai.seo_question: What does the scent of incense on the Imam signify in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi* highlights the sensory refinement of Imam al-Hassan al-Askari (peace be upon him), whose scent of incense (*tajmeer*) served as a subtle sign of his presence and dignity. In Shia tradition, such physical attributes are often viewed as manifestations of inner purity and the Imam’s connection to the divine, reinforcing the concept that the Imams embody both spiritual and aesthetic excellence.
